edges.parent_basis:
The decree names the constitution it executes, by title, by pope and by day: the
texts belonging to the Roman Missal having been approved through the Apostolic
Constitution Missale Romanum given by the Supreme Pontiff Paul VI on 3 April
1969. An act that recites what it is executing has drawn its own edge.

before.incipit: Munda cor meum, ut supra, et Iube, Ddmine, benedicere.
before.name: Oratio

cited.basis: Established by search on the 1970 side and by a cross-reference only on the 1962 side; see the note.
cited.note:
THE PRAYER IS IN BOTH BOOKS AND ITS STATE IS STILL NOT ESTABLISHED, which is
what `unrecorded` is for.

An accent-normalised search of 1970-missale-romanum-typica for `munda cor meum
ac labia mea` returns the prayer at lines 21303 and 26387 [verified], so it
survived. But the 1962 unit here was read from a CROSS-REFERENCE -- the Benziger
book prints `Munda cor meum, ut supra` at this point and the prayer itself
stands earlier -- so this file has never read the 1962 words. Two texts cannot be
compared when one of them was not read, and carrying the unit forward unchanged
would assert an identity nobody established.

So the unit leaves the liturgy at this station and a marker takes its place. The
fix is cheap and is not guesswork: read the Munda cor meum where the 1962 book
actually prints it.

before.incipit: av&bo inter innoc^ntes manus meas: et circumdabo alt£re tuiun, D6mine
before.name: Psalmus 25

cited.basis:
THE SLOT SURVIVES AND THE PSALM IN IT DOES NOT. The washing of hands is still
there and the verse said at it is no longer Psalm 25. An accent-normalised
whole-file search of 1970-missale-romanum-typica for `lavabo inter innocentes`
returns zero; a search for `lava me` returns the verse at lines 21490 and 26498,
in the Order of Mass [verified].

This is `replaced` and not `absent` followed by `added`, because the unit is the
washing of hands and it did not go away. The new words are NOT reproduced here:
the incipit is withheld under the rights position on the 1970 book, and the
emitted repository prints `[incipit withheld: ...]` so that a reader can tell a
withheld text from a text nobody read.

before.incipit: Confiteor Deo omnipotenti, be&tse Mariae semper Virgini, be&I to Michae I i Arch&ngelo, beato Iofinni Baptistee, sanctis Ap6stolis Petro et Paulo, 6mnibus Sanctis, et vobis, fratres
before.name: Confiteor

cited.basis:
The Confiteor survives and its form does not. An accent-normalised search of
1970-missale-romanum-typica for `confiteor deo omnipotenti` returns two hits, at
lines 21150 and one other, so the prayer stands; and the 1962 unit's own
enumeration -- blessed Mary ever Virgin, blessed Michael the Archangel, blessed
John the Baptist, the holy Apostles Peter and Paul -- is not in the 1970 text at
that place, where `et vobis fratres` follows `omnipotenti` directly [verified].

The new form's words are withheld for the same reason as the Lavabo above. What
is recorded is a difference established by searching, not a transcription.

before.incipit: Iud ica me, Deus, et disc&rne causam meam de gente non sancta: ab h6mine infquo, et dol6so 6rue me.
before.name: Psalmus 42

cited.basis:
The psalm is gone from the preparation. An accent-normalised whole-file search
of 1970-missale-romanum-typica for `iudica me deus et discerne` returns ONE hit,
at line 11491, AND IT IS NOT THIS UNIT: the surrounding text reads `ant ad
introitum ps iudica me deus et discerne causam meam de gente non sancta`, which
is the psalm serving as an ENTRANCE ANTIPHON on a day of the year, not the
prayers at the foot of the altar [verified]. A count-only search would have
recorded the unit as surviving.
